source_text: Intellegis retectas esse Manichaei dogmatis medullas, quibus fides vestra concrescit. Iam vero nos id est catholicos pergit arguere: Quare vide, quam stulti sunt, qui dicunt hoc figmentum a Deo bono esse conditum, quod certi sunt ab spiritu concupiscentiae gigni.
pass_a_gloss: You understand that the marrows of the Manichaean's dogma have been uncovered, by which your faith grows together. Now truly he proceeds to argue us, that is catholics: For which reason see how stupid they are who say this figment has been founded by the good God, which they are certain is generated from the spirit of desire.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: You understand that the innermost substance of Mani’s doctrine has been exposed—the substance from which your faith grows. Now he goes on to accuse us, that is, catholics: ‘See, then, how foolish they are who say this bodily formation was created by the good God, when they know it is generated by the spirit of desire.’

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
